IADC 111 – 637 CODE MAPPING

Choose the IADC group from the formation.

The wrong bit slows the right mast. Groups run from very soft ground to hard abrasive rock.

IADC 111, 113, 115, 117

Very soft ground

Used in clay, silt and mud-like soils. This series has the longest teeth. Available with ball-journal, felt-journal and felt friction bearings.

IADC 211, 213, 215, 217

Moderately soft formations

Advances quickly in gravelly and alluvial ground. Available with ball-journal, felt-journal and felt friction bearings.

IADC 231, 233, 234, 235, 236, 237

Abrasive formations

Closely spaced hardened teeth, diamond-reinforced for abrasive formations. Ball-journal, felt-journal and felt friction bearings.

IADC 415, 417

Soft rock and lower formations

Should be run at slow speed. Felt-journal and felt friction bearings.

IADC 435, 437

Soft rocks

Smaller primary tooth tips for faster cutting. Use at slow speed. Felt-journal and felt friction bearings.

IADC 515, 517

Soft to medium-hard formations

Shorter, more closely spaced teeth. Use at medium speed. Felt-journal and felt friction bearings.

IADC 535, 537

Medium-hard and abrasive formations

Shorter tooth structure for harder rock. Used at medium speed. Felt-journal and felt friction bearings.

IADC 635, 637

Hard and abrasive formations

Short conical teeth for crushing under continuous weight. Used at high speed. Ball-journal, felt-journal and felt friction bearings.
